description: Bounded three-trial nearest-union probe of the shared FF-input map
proposal: Family: parameter tying. Current retained frontier is 1,435 parameters at 99.090000%, a +0.090000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 92 prior macro-attempts in this family and 720 prior micro-trials. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0194/micro-0001 at 1,435 parameters and 99.09%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0194/micro-0002, an FF-output union discarded at 98.91%. This macro tests at most three sequential minimum-distance scalar unions in the depth-shared FF-input map, excluding every unchanged pair already rejected at this site. Hypothesis: nonlinear feature construction may retain near-duplicate scalars after the complementary FF-output boundary was reached. This is more informative than the nearest untested alternative because each micro-trial selects the least-distorting eligible FF-input union, separating this tensor site from the just-observed FF-output failure while bounding adaptation to three official trials. Stop at the first discard/error, exhaustion, or declared cap; official acceptance and rollback remain solely controlled by the runner.
summary: All three bounded FF-input unions qualified, reducing the retained frontier from 1,435 to 1,432 parameters; the final authorized trial retained 99.060000%. The automation stopped exactly at its declared three-trial cap.
